# Everyone Film Editorial 1.4.1 — portrait captions

Template `everyone-casting` 1.4.1 is the 1.4.0 Floward cast shortlist layout ([1.4.0 composition](1.4.0-composition.md))
plus, under each person's portrait, **only their name, age and height**. Owner request after testing: "In the template,
I want only the name, age and height to be shown that's it. If height is not there it won't be displayed."

- Composer: `packages/templates/versions/1.4.1/compose-casting.ts` (`portraitCaption`, `captionHeight`); geometry:
  `castCaption` in `packages/templates/versions/1.4.1/layouts.ts`. Every other rule (pages, Main/Backup labels,
  option chunks, scenes, notes, silhouettes, cover, closing, no PDF video links) is 1.4.0's, unchanged.
- 1.4.0 stays byte-identical (registry `b4fbd16f…`); saved 1.4.0 versions keep printing without captions.
- Migration m23 (`20261119110000_m23_editorial_template_1_4_1.sql`) registers 1.4.1 and admits it wherever m19 admits
  1.4.0. It does **not** change the Settings default; a Studio manager selects 1.4.1 in Settings.

## Caption content

| Line | Source (captured slide wording) | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `fields.name_or_id` (the name, else the casting ID) | Omitted when not provided. Wraps to at most two lines. |
| Age \| height | `fields.age_or_range` as supplied, then the height from `fields.height_measurements` | Each part only when provided, joined by ` \| `; the line is omitted when neither is. |

"Provided" means not blank and not the review's `Not provided` / `Pending` text: captions never print either.
A person whose picture is the silhouette (no picture, or intentionally empty) is still captioned; a missing Main or
Backup (the silhouette of nobody) and an open role's Pending page are not.

### Height

`fields.height_measurements` is free text (for example the archive's `Height: 173; weight: 77. Units not stated.`).
Only the height is shown, never the weight or another measurement, and the unit only when one is stated:

| Measurements | Caption height |
| --- | --- |
| `Height: 173; weight: 77. Units not stated.` | `173` |
| `180 cm` | `180 cm` |
| `Chest 90, height 182 cm` | `182 cm` |
| `1.73m` / `5'11"` / `180 cm, 75 kg` / `173` | `1.73 m` / `5'11"` / `180 cm` / `173` |
| `weight 70 kg`, `77 kg`, `Height: unknown`, `Height / Measurements`, empty | nothing (line shows the age only, or is omitted) |

Grammar: the value after the word `height` (`:`, `-`, `=` or `is` may follow), or a field that starts with a length
(a number with a length unit, feet and inches) or is only a number. ASCII classes and explicit word boundaries only;
the SQL mirror `eps.editorial141_has_height` embeds the composer's two regular expressions verbatim
(`tests/worker/editorial-1-4-1-sql-mirror.test.ts` checks both the text and the behaviour).

## Geometry and type

Existing tokens only: the name is `castName` (General Sans Regular 35, the reference "casting person label"), the
age | height line is `caption` (General Sans Light 30). Both are centred in the portrait column (464 wide); the caption
is a top-anchored stack starting at y 883 (reference BP-46 name position; portraits end at 866), so a one-line name
pulls the age | height line up. The tallest caption (two name lines + one line) ends at y 1008, clear of the note row
(y 1030) and the page number. Captions never change the pages, pictures, sources or page numbers (tested on the
Floward structure and 300 random reviews).

## Fit and proof

- Each line is a fit-measured region of its person (`data-fit-field` `presentation.caption_name` /
  `presentation.caption_details`, `data-fit-source` = the person's slide): a third name line is a vertical overflow,
  an age | height line wider than the column a horizontal one. Review blocks generation with "The name under the
  portrait does not fit on two lines." / "The age and height under the portrait do not fit on one line."
  (`eps.review_fit_message`). Type is never shrunk.
- Captions are checked PDF text regions. `eps.editorial_deck_counts_1_4_1` = the 1.4.0 mirror (pages, pictures,
  silhouettes) plus the caption regions per printed occurrence of each role; agreement with the composer on 301
  synthetic snapshots.
- PowerPoint: the caption is one native text box per person with two centred paragraphs (the name wraps and pushes
  the age | height line down, as in the PDF).

Visual evidence (synthetic people, PDF rasterised with pdftoppm and the PPTX exported by PowerPoint): `.local/cycle8/template/`.
